newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: US Marines fly out foreigners fleeing Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: US Marines fly out foreigners fleeing Sierra Leone.

text.p: U.S. Marines using 15 helicopters evacuated 900 foreigners fleeing violence in Sierra Leone on Friday despite orders by coup leaders closing the country's airspace.
Nigeria flew in jeeps, armoured personnel carriers and more troops for an expected regional intervention to restore the civilian president and there were signs that Ghana and Guinea would join in.

Washington said it was suspending the operation of its embassy in Freetown, where military and diplomatic sources said rebel commanders had joined the coup leaders and were rejecting any mediation to try to reverse the overthrow of the elected government.

In Ghana's capital Accra, a cabinet minister said President Jerry Rawlings was in telephone contact with Sierra Leone's new military leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah, trying to persuade him to negotiate a political settlement.

By 3.30 p.m. (1530 GMT), 15 C-46 Sea Knight helicopters running non-stop shuttles had ferried all 900 waiting evacuees, including more than 300 U.S.-passport holders, to the U.S. Navy helicopter carrier Kearsarge lying 12 miles off the coast.
What started as the evacuation of American citizens to the Kearsarge quickly turned into a rush to leave the capital.
"We'll try to make sure that everybody who has to go is taken to the ship," said Marine Lieutenant-Colonel Tom Greenwood.
There was no sign of the Sierra Leone military, whose leaders ousted the elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah last Sunday prompting an international outcry.
Regional power Nigeria has built up a force in Freetown over the past week and is expected to move against Koromah.
Ghana said it was consulting with Nigeria and Guinea on the situation and prepared troop transport planes, officially to evacuate Ghanaian nationals living in Sierra Leone.

Nigeria leads the ECOMOG regional intervention force sent to Liberia in 1990, which also has some troops in Sierra Leone Diplomats said the closure of land, sea and air borders, announced by the Freetown authorities on Thursday night, was to stop the Nigerian buildup. Sierra Leonean sources said it was also an attempt to impede the departure of Westerners to minimise chances of military action.
One report said Guinea had flown in 500 men on Thursday night but this could not immediately be confirmed.

Military and diplomatic sources said leaders of the rebel Revolutionary United Front (RUF), who had been waging a guerrilla campaign since 1991 but were now allied to the coupmakers, entered the capital two days ago.

"The RUF leaders came out of the bush and entered the town. Now it seems the soldiers have got more than they bargained for because the rebels are now calling the shots," a West African peacekeeping officer said.
A diplomat involved with attempts to strike a deal with Koromah said a veteran politician sent to mediation talks at military headquarters on Thursday night found 50 rebel commanders there.
"They were sitting with the coup leaders, who had their military ranks stripped from their uniforms," the diplomat said, quoting the politician.
"It is a serious problem because the rebels have rejected any mediation. They say they are ready to fight to the end and are prepared for anything," he said.
The Kearsarge was due to sail for Conakry, capital of neighbouring Guinea, where evacuees would make their own travel arrangements.

In Washington, State Department spokeswoman Julie Reside said: "We have decided that we are suspending the operation of our embassy in Freetown." She could not say whether all embassy staff had evacuated the premises.
In London, nearly 400 Westerners arrived on Friday after being evacuated. Some spoke of fearing death after Sunday's coup as soldiers rammed through gates and then looted their houses.
Military sources said the evacuations were the main reason the Nigerians had not yet acted despite support for their role by the United States and the regional bloc, ECOWAS.
The coup leaders have shown increasing signs of anxiety as foreign countries accelerate the evacuation of their nationals. Former colonial ruler Britain completed its airlift on Thursday.
